subject: Tenant egress proofing + fallthrough playbook
messages:

Cc: irene_choi@redwood.com, naomi_feldman@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Tenant egress options / proofing ask

Hey Mateo + team,

Quick background: we're moving a subset of Acme Financial workloads into a private Redwood deployment (per-tenant VPCs on our colo). Compliance requires strict egress control: no unapproved outbound IPs, auditable proxies, and a documented fallback if tenant egress fails.

Can you share a recommended approach for:
- tenant-specific egress (SNAT vs upstream proxy)
- a fallthrough path that preserves auditability (if tenant proxy is unreachable)
- a minimal runbook we can ship to our security/compliance reviewers

I've attached a sheet with our current NAT/ACLs (acme-current-network.xlsx). If you can point to a simple diagram and a short checklist we can review internally, that would speed things up. We're hoping to have acceptance criteria by the end of next week.

Thanks,
Tom
Tom Weber
Head of Infra, Acme Financial

Attachments: acme-current-network.xlsx (spreadsheet)
From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Tom Weber <t.weber@acme.com>
Cc: irene_choi@redwood.com, naomi_feldman@redwood.com
Date: 2028-03-21T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Tenant egress options / proofing ask

Tom — thanks, this is helpful. Draft response / proposal below; I'm also sharing a diagram and an early runbook in Drive (link below).

Summary proposal (high level):
1) Per-tenant egress via lightweight proxy cluster inside the tenant VPCs (transparent HTTP proxy + TLS termination for audit).
   - Benefits: preserves per-tenant auditing, easier policy enforcement, no noisy SNAT tables per host.
   - Fallback: when the tenant proxy cannot reach the internet (network outage, process crash), traffic is routed to a managed shared egress cluster in the management VPC. The fallthrough path must NAT at the shared egress and tag logs with tenant id to preserve auditability.

2) Control plane connectivity: the Redwood control plane (management VPC) will peer privately to tenant VPCs using routed VPC peering. Control plane APIs (agent registration, key provisioning) stay on a separate /24 and are only reachable from the tenant side over a managed tunnel.

3) Routing: tenant routing advertises 0.0.0.0/0 to the local proxy (default route). The proxy performs policy checks; a local BGP session is not required for most customers — we prefer route-based fallthrough via SDN routes to avoid BGP complexity. For customers requiring BGP, we support an optional BGP session (see risk note below).

4) Audit and logs: all egress flows that hit the shared fallthrough must include tenant metadata (x-tenant-id header or flow-label) before SNAT so logs in the shared egress can be correlated back to tenant.

Canary + acceptance criteria (short):
- Canary tenant with low criticality enabled for proxy + fallthrough routing for 48h.
- Verify per-token and per-connection logs show tenant-id and user-agent.
- Confirm MTU/fragmentation behavior for large responses (file downloads) between tenant proxy and shared egress (no > 1500 drop).
- Simulate tenant proxy failure and verify failover to shared egress within 30s.

Next steps / owners:
- Mateo: upload diagrams and draft runbook to Drive (done) — https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cAcme-Egress-Design
- Irene: validate control-plane port allowances and key provisioning flow (Irene, can you confirm by EOD Thu?)
- Naomi: schedule network validation tests with Acme SEs (Naomi, can you propose times?)

Attachments (sent): tenant-egress-fallthrough-v1.pdf (diagram), runbook-draft.md

Notes / risks: if we rely on SNAT-only (no proxy), application-level auditing is weaker and you may need to push logs out-of-band. BGP sessions add operational complexity and are only recommended for customers with existing BGP device expertise.

--
Mateo Alvarez
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: tenant-egress-fallthrough-v1.pdf (diagram), runbook-draft.md
From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>

Date: 2028-03-22T08:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Tenant egress options / proofing ask

Thanks for the draft — quick operational comments below (quoting Mateo where helpful):

> Control plane connectivity: the Redwood control plane (management VPC) will peer privately to tenant VPCs using routed VPC peering.

- Confirming: peering uses encrypted tunnels (mTLS between agents) and we do not expose control-plane APIs to the public internet. We need to ensure cert propagation happens over an out-of-band channel during onboarding (KMS rotate + signed cert bundle).
- Action: I'll run the cert-propagation sequence in staging Thursday and report back.

> Routing / MTU note: Confirm MTU/fragmentation behavior for large responses (file downloads).

- We've seen 1420 MTU hairpins in one colo vendor when GRE encapsulation is present. Recommend the runbook include an MTU verification step (ping -s, file transfer checks) and a mitigation path (adjust MSS, enable PMTU probing).

Action items for network:
- Net team (cc'd): validate that shared egress labels can be injected into flows prior to SNAT (we use an HTTP header for app traffic; flow-label for non-HTTP).
- Document how we handle UDP flows that need NAT + tenant attribution.

I'll attach a small patch with the control plane port list and the cert rotation commands.

Onwards,
Irene
Irene Choi
Director, Platform Ops — Redwood Inference
